SWARM KEY SHUFFLE - RELAY PROTOCOL

The relay is a line-oriented TCP service. Connect with `nc <host> <port>`;
the banner lists the available commands.

KEY MATERIAL
    - e = d^-1 mod phi(N).
    - The clearance token is 16 uniformly random bytes, encrypted raw:
          c = token^e mod N
      Submit the token as lowercase hex. It is independent of the flag; a
      correct token authorizes the relay to release the flag.

SESSION LIFETIME
    - A session you never AUTH against expires after about 2 minutes, so
      abandoned handshakes do not pile up on the relay.
    - Once you send an AUTH for a session, it stays usable for the relay's
      full 30-minute window, or until you exhaust its attempts.
    - `KEY` can be called again at any time, subject to a short per-connection
      cooldown and a per-connection session cap, if you need fresh key
      material.

SUBMISSION FORMAT
    - AUTH <session> <token-hex>
    - Malformed token hex is rejected with ERROR and does not consume an
      attempt. A well-formed but incorrect token consumes one of the
      session's attempts.
